title: Dynamics & Newton's Laws
confusion: ❌ 'The normal force is always mg.' ✅ N = mg only on a horizontal surface with no vertical acceleration.
❌ 'Friction always opposes motion.' ✅ Friction opposes RELATIVE motion between surfaces, not necessarily the body's motion.
❌ 'Action and reaction forces cancel each other.' ✅ They act on DIFFERENT bodies, so they never cancel in a single FBD.
❌ 'Heavier bodies slide slower down a slope.' ✅ $a = g(\sin \theta - \mu \cos \theta)$ has no mass term.
notes: **Newton's first law:** A body at rest stays at rest and a body in motion stays in uniform motion unless acted on by a net external force. **Inertia** is the tendency to resist change in state of motion; mass is a measure of inertia.

**Newton's second law:** $\sum \vec{F} = m\vec{a}$. The rate of change of momentum is proportional to the applied force and takes place in the direction of the force. $F = ma$ applies when mass is constant.

**Newton's third law:** For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction. Forces always act in pairs on **different** bodies, so they never cancel each other out in a single free body diagram (FBD).
**Impulse:** $\vec{J} = \vec{F}\Delta t = \Delta \vec{p}$. It represents the change in momentum. Graphically, it is the area under the force-time curve.
**Momentum:** $\vec{p} = m\vec{v}$. Conserved in an isolated system where $\sum \vec{F}_{ext} = 0$.
1. **Static Friction ($f_s$):** Acts when there is no relative motion between surfaces. It adjusts its magnitude up to a maximum value: $0 \le f_s \le \mu_s N$.
2. **Kinetic Friction ($f_k$):** Acts when there is relative sliding motion. It is generally constant in magnitude: $f_k = \mu_k N$.
2. Draw all external forces acting on it (Gravity, Normal, Tension, Friction, Applied Forces).
3. Do NOT include reaction forces acting on OTHER bodies.
4. Apply $\sum F_x = ma_x$ and $\sum F_y = ma_y$.
